slides.0.title: Geography, climate and the ocean
slides.0.subtitle: Cold current, sea wind and a Mediterranean climate
slides.1.title: Location and climate pattern
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Southern-hemisphere vineyards
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Viticulture lies mainly between about 27 and 34 degrees south; coastal areas are seldom more than 50 km from the ocean
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Mediterranean climate
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters, with rain concentrated in June–August (1,000 mm or more on seaward slopes, about 500 mm in the Swartland and inland Paarl)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Mostly dryland or supplementary irrigation
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Because rain falls mainly in winter, most viticulture is dryland or supplementally irrigated; harvest falls in the southern-hemisphere months of February–April
slides.1.content: Remember: a Mediterranean climate with winter rain, and seasons opposite to the northern hemisphere.
slides.2.title: Ocean and wind
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The Benguela Current
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A cold-water current flowing north from the Antarctic along the west coast, cooling the coastal air
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The Cape Doctor
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A strong south-easterly wind blowing from September to March that lowers temperatures by several degrees and reduces disease pressure
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Onshore breezes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Onshore breezes moderate summer heat in Stellenbosch, Constantia, Durbanville and Darling; inland Paarl, Wellington and Tulbagh are warmer
slides.2.content: The cold current and sea winds are why South Africa feels cooler than its latitude suggests.
slides.3.title: Soils and climate change
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Four signature soils
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Decomposed granite (Stellenbosch foothills, Franschhoek), Malmesbury shale (Swartland), Table Mountain Sandstone (high slopes above Constantia and Hottentots-Holland), Bokkeveld shale (Durbanville)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Earlier harvests
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Harvest dates have moved roughly two weeks earlier since the 1990s
slides.3.content: Soils, altitude, aspect and a warming trend are the common backdrop for the regional lessons ahead.
A south-easterly wind from September to March that cools and reduces disease.
